title: Regular ordinary pullback of potential complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $r:P\to X$ be a regular morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring], where regular means flat with geometrically regular fibres (each fibre remains regular after every finite residue-field extension) [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $\delta_X$ be a dimension function and $(K,(p_x))$ a pinned putative dualizing complex [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Then
$$\delta_r(t)=\delta_X(r(t))-\dim\mathcal O_{P_{r(t)},t}$$
is a dimension function, and ordinary inverse image $r^*K$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] has natural putative pinnings for $\delta_r$. It is potential if $K$ is potential. The pinnings commute with composition of regular morphisms and with localization. They are defined fibrewise by the canonical supported-cohomology comparison with $r_x^*R\Gamma_xK$ and the inverse regular Gysin classes on the regular fibre. In particular, on a regular scheme the constant sheaf, with inverse Gysin pinnings for the function $-\operatorname{codim}$, pulls back with these same inverse Gysin pinnings. Here codimension at a point of a regular scheme is the dimension of its local ring. This assertion concerns ordinary $r^*$, and does not assume that $r$ is of finite type or compactifiable.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.1.1 and Remark 4.1.3; Lemmas 4.3.1.1 and 4.3.1.2 for the fibrewise pinning and its regular normalization

proof.text:
For a geometric specialization $t'\rightsquigarrow t$, put $x'=r(t')$, $x=r(t)$ and $b(v)=\dim\mathcal O_{P_{r(v)},v}$. By [lem-per-regular-specialization-geometry],
$$c_P(t',t)=c_X(x',x)+b(t)-b(t').$$
Factor $x'\rightsquigarrow x$ into immediate specializations, as allowed by [lem-per-general-costalk-transitions]. The definition of a dimension function in [def-per-potential-dualizing] gives $\delta_X(x')-\delta_X(x)=c_X(x',x)$ by summing its drop of one along that chain (and gives zero for a codimension-zero geometric isomorphism). Substituting in the displayed identity yields
$$\delta_r(t')-\delta_r(t)=c_P(t',t).$$
In particular it is one for an immediate specialization upstairs, proving that $\delta_r$ is a dimension function.

source.place: XIV, Proposition 2.5.4, expressed using the generic-fibre specialization geometry; XVII, Lemmas 4.3.2.4–4.3.2.6

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and put $X_x=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $P_x=P\times_XX_x$, and $F=P\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. Write $i:F\hookrightarrow P_x$, $q:F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ and $j:P_x\to P$. Apply [lem-per-regular-closed-support-base-change] after localization of the regular map $r$ to the closed point of $X_x$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $q^*R\Gamma_xK\cong i^!j^*r^*K$. The given $p_x$ therefore identifies this last object with $\Lambda_F(\delta_X(x))[2\delta_X(x)]$. The fibre $F$ is regular by the regular-morphism hypothesis. Its affine coordinate rings are localizations of quotients of affine coordinate rings of $P$: on affine charts with ring map $A\to B$ and $x$ represented by $\mathfrak p$, they are localizations of $B/\mathfrak p B$ by the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Thus they and their local rings are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], applied to the finite-type quotient and its multiplicative localization. These are Noetherian as part of excellence. Ordinary inverse image preserves the bounded-below condition by the exactness theorem [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact].

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.1.1, first half; Corollary 4.2.3; excellence stability as in Stacks Tag 07QU, more-algebra.tex lemma-finite-type-over-excellent

proof.text:
For $t\in F$ put $c=\dim\mathcal O_{F,t}$ and $a=\delta_X(x)$. Work on the local scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{F,t}$, which is Noetherian, excellent and regular by step 2. The closed-point inclusion $t\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{F,t}$ is a closed immersion between regular affine Noetherian excellent schemes, so [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] gives the absolute-purity isomorphism $\operatorname{Cl}_{t\hookrightarrow F}:\Lambda(-c)[-2c]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_t\Lambda_F$. By [lem-per-regular-constant-gysin-potential] with $m=a$, the inverses of these classes, tensored by $(a)[2a]$, are the pinnings of the pinned potential complex $\Lambda_F(a)[2a]$ for $a-\dim\mathcal O_{F,-}$ in degree $a-c$ at $t$. Define the desired pinning by the composite
$$R\Gamma_t(r^*K)\cong R\Gamma_t(i^!j^*r^*K)\cong R\Gamma_t(q^*R\Gamma_xK)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_t(q^*p_x)}R\Gamma_t\Lambda_F(a)[2a]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Cl}_{t\hookrightarrow F}^{-1}(a)[2a]}\Lambda(a-c)[2a-2c].$$
Here the first identification is supported composition after localization; all identifications and their coherence are included in [lem-per-regular-closed-support-base-change]. Since $a-c=\delta_r(t)$, these are putative pinnings. Each point lies on its specified fibre, so this defines a pinning at every point with no gluing choice. Naturality in pinning-preserving maps follows by applying the natural comparison and the fixed inverse Gysin map to those maps.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.1.1, second half; Proposition 2.4.1.1 (inverse Gysin convention), and Proposition 2.4.4.1

proof.text: Check regular normalization locally at $t\in P$ and $x=r(t)$ when $X$ and $P$ are regular and the input pinnings are inverse Gysin pinnings on $\Lambda_X$. Let $c=\operatorname{codim}_X(x)$ and $d=\operatorname{codim}_{F}(t)$. The Gysin base-change assertion of [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] identifies $r^*\operatorname{Cl}_{x\hookrightarrow X}$ with $\operatorname{Cl}_{F\hookrightarrow P_x}$ under the supported comparison. Its composition assertion then identifies the product of this class and $\operatorname{Cl}_{t\hookrightarrow F}$ with $\operatorname{Cl}_{t\hookrightarrow P}$; the codimensions add in this composition. Taking inverses, the composite in step 3 is exactly $\operatorname{Cl}_{t\hookrightarrow P}^{-1}$. All class morphisms here are closed immersions between regular affine local schemes, or their localization restrictions, as allowed by that node. The change-of-base map is regular, which is all its base-change clause requires; it need not be finite type. This gives the asserted normalization for the constant sheaf, with dimension function $-\operatorname{codim}_P$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.1.2, including the product of the two Gysin classes; XVI, Theorem 2.5.12

proof.text: Assume now that $K$ is potential, and fix a geometric specialization $t'\rightsquigarrow t$ over $x'\rightsquigarrow x$. Use [lem-per-regular-specialization-geometry] to choose the commutative square with fibre-generic points $\eta'$ over $x'$ and $\eta$ over $x$. For the vertical edges $\eta'\rightsquigarrow t'$ and $\eta\rightsquigarrow t$, step 2 identifies the fibre-supported complex with the constant twist-shift determined by $p_{x'}$ and $p_x$, respectively. With exactly these inverse-Gysin pinnings that fibre complex is potential by [lem-per-regular-constant-gysin-potential], applied to the regular Noetherian excellent fibre (step 2) with $m=\delta_X(x)$, respectively $m=\delta_X(x')$. The closed-support and localization compatibility of [lem-per-general-costalk-transitions] identifies its transitions with the transitions on $r^*K$. Factoring a vertical edge into immediate specializations and composing therefore shows that its transition, under the pinnings of step 3, is the identity of $\Lambda$ with the required twist. [lem-per-regular-constant-gysin-potential] imposes no connectedness, so none is required of a fibre.

source.place: XVII, Section 4.3.3, the two vertical sides of the square; Lemma 4.3.1.1 and Theorem 3.1.2

proof.text: Factor $x'\rightsquigarrow x$ into immediate specializations. The lifting assertion of [lem-per-regular-specialization-geometry] factors the top edge $\eta'\rightsquigarrow\eta$ through fibre-generic points over that chain. Apply [lem-per-regular-pinnings-low-base-codimension] to each lifted edge, since its image has codimension one; a codimension-zero image is also covered by that lemma. Compose using [lem-per-general-costalk-transitions]. The top edge therefore also becomes the identity under the pinnings. Transitivity applied to the commutative square says that its two composite transition maps agree. Both vertical maps and the top map have just become identities, so the bottom transition $t'\rightsquigarrow t$ becomes the identity too. In particular every immediate bottom specialization respects the specified pinnings. These costalks are isomorphic to a shifted one-dimensional $\mathbf F_\ell$-space by step 3. Maps between the matching shifts of such objects are determined by their map on the single nonzero cohomology group (a complex with one cohomology object is its shift). Hence the cohomological identity is the equality in $D^+(\mathbf F_\ell)$ required by [def-per-potential-dualizing]. This proves potentiality, including when the image of an immediate specialization has higher codimension.

source.place: XVII, Section 4.3.3, the top edge and the commutative-square argument, using Lemmas 4.3.2.1 and 4.3.2.5 and Theorem 3.1.2

proof.text: For regular maps $Q\xrightarrow{s}P\xrightarrow{r}X$, check the two constructions at a point $u\in Q$ over $x\in X$. The pasting and supported-composition clauses of [lem-per-regular-closed-support-base-change] identify both constructions with the ones on $Q_x\xrightarrow{s_x}P_x\to x$ after applying the same input pinning $p_x$. Thus on these fibres the input is the same constant complex $\Lambda(\delta_X(x))[2\delta_X(x)]$. Each fibre scheme over $x$ is regular. Step 4 says that pulling its inverse Gysin pinnings along the regular $s_x$ gives its inverse Gysin pinnings again. Applying the common twist and shift therefore makes the iterated pinnings equal the direct pinnings, under $s^*r^*K\cong(rs)^*K$. This argument uses only the individual input $p_x$, so applies to putative $K$ as well as potential $K$. Finally localization of source or target restricts the same supported comparison, $p_x$, and Gysin class; localization compatibility in [lem-per-regular-closed-support-base-change] and [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] makes the displayed composites equal after restriction. This proves the localization clause for the specified maps.
